basis: Umbrella disorder defined by disease of the renal glomerulus; immune mechanisms are not universal.
Disease of the coronary arteries; no additional organ damage is intrinsic across the group.
Venom directly disrupts neuronal function; cardiac conduction abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Local erythema is transient; pulmonary edema occurs in 5-29%.
Dysplasminogenemia is an inherited fibrinolytic coagulation protein disorder; type I mucosal lesions should not be extrapolated to type II.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with cortical dysplasia in 30-79%; listed ocular, cardiac and other structural abnormalities are individually occasional.
Peroxisomal plasmalogen disorder causing rhizomelic chondrodysplasia and cataracts; neurodevelopmental impairment occurs in most affected patients.
Congenital muscular dystrophy with impaired intellectual development and an inherited glycosylation defect; reported seizures and white-matter abnormalities support CNS disease.
Autism is a neurodevelopmental disorder; this concept denotes severe support needs.
Inherited bile acid conjugation defect. Fat malabsorption does not establish intestinal tissue damage; hepatic injury is not established as common.
Classic Zellweger disease affects peroxisomal metabolism, brain and liver; renal cystic dysplasia is common (>30%). Skeletal and ocular manifestations omitted at the cap.
Congenital absence or severe underdevelopment of lung tissue; associated anomalies are not universal defining organ disease.
Hereditary degeneration of distal motor neurons or axons. Muscle wasting is secondary to denervation, rather than a separate primary myopathy.
Neurodevelopmental disease with seizures and callosal abnormalities; hypodontia affects 3/7 (43%). Hearing impairment in 2/7 (29%) is below threshold.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with drug-resistant seizures and cognitive and motor impairment.
Adenomatous neoplasm arising in the colon or rectum.
Inflammation of the biceps tendon sheath; an autoimmune or infectious mechanism is not inherent.
Inherited pantothenate/CoA metabolic defect causing brain iron-associated neurodegeneration. Retinopathy, blindness and optic atrophy occur in only 1-4%.
Dental malocclusion involving protruding upper incisors; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Renal tubulopathy with electrolyte disturbance and anhidrosis; lacrimal dysfunction in 13/13. Salivary dysfunction/xerostomia in 13/13 omitted at the four-axis cap.
Immune-mediated auricular and joint chondritis; supplied HPO reports vasculitis in 80-99%. Airway damage (30-79%) and ocular involvement omitted at the four-axis cap.
Granulomatous inflammation directly damages arterial walls; this is an inflammatory vasculitis.
Neurodevelopmental delay and congenital cardiac malformations characterize the syndrome; frequencies of additional ocular and skeletal defects are insufficient.
Enterovirus infection umbrella; digestive-tract replication does not establish common intestinal damage. Neurologic and cardiac disease occur in subsets.
The named syndrome comprises ocular colobomata, a unilobar lung anomaly and a congenital heart defect; further characterization is unavailable.
Neoplasm originating in the parathyroid endocrine gland; hormonal excess and downstream organ injury are not universal across the tumor group.
